items.originalTitle: 'Hello world': Google's space AI writes first Haiku, Sundar Pichai lauds Project Suncatcher milestone
items.originalSummary: Google on Friday reached a historic milestone as its prototype satellite launched earlier this month sent back its first AI-generated response. This is seen as the tech giant's first step towards exploring Artificial intelligence in space. The response was a haiku about life in orbit and marked the first successful machine learning response from a data centre-class Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) operating in space. While it is an early test, it still brings Google's Project Suncatcher a step closer to its long-term ambition of building AI data centres in space. "This week, we reached our 'Hello World' milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data centre-class TPU in orbit," Google said in a statement on Friday. A ‘hello world’ milestone for Project Suncatcher 🚀 After launching our prototype satellite a few weeks ago, we’ve now successfully sent a command up to orbit, booted up the TPU, ran the prompt, and received our first complete response back on earth - a haiku! https://t.co/kOFmETUskm — Sundar Pichai (@sundarpichai) October 30, 2026 "During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed by Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success," it furthered. The haiku shared by the prototype satellite is as follows: - Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. - "Our chips have officially earned their space wings — an important achievement on the long road ahead for this cosmic moonshot," Google concluded in its update. Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai also released a statement, lauding the historic milestone. About Project Suncatcher The prototype in question carries four Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs. Google designed these chips for machine learning and already uses them in data centres on Earth. It is pertinent to note that the satellite runs an onboard version of the Gemma AI model. Due to heat-management limits, the chips are only expected to run the model for 15 minutes and can only handle simple requests. In the next stage, the firm would now focus on how the processors cope with the conditions of space. Google plans to test their performance under thermal stress and radiation exposure. Radiation has always been a concern for the developers since it can cause what engineers call “bit flips”. The radiation can corrupt data without necessarily setting off standard monitoring systems. It is pertinent to note that the Project Suncatcher is a long-term research effort by Google to explore whether space could eventually support large-scale machine learning infrastructure. Google is exploring whether connected satellite groups could use that energy to handle larger AI workloads. The company plans to test twin interconnected satellites in 2027.

items.title: 「星光滋養我的核心」：Google衛星晶片寫下了第一首太空資料中心詩
items.originalTitle: ‘Starlight feeds my core’: Google satellite chip pens first-ever space data center poem
items.originalSummary: Google has successfully run its first machine learning prompt on a satellite-mounted processor, bringing its space-based computing experiment closer to reality. The prototype spacecraft generated an AI response from orbit using Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).The achievement marks an early milestone for Project Suncatcher, Google’s research initiative exploring large-scale computing infrastructure in space. Engineers launched the satellite on October 1 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. It shared the ride with more than 100 other spacecraft.Google confirmed that its onboard systems completed initial checks after approximately three weeks of commissioning. The team has now demonstrated that an orbital TPU can handle basic machine learning workloads.First AI response from orbitDuring a ground-station communication window, engineers transmitted a prompt to Google’s Gemma 4 open model. They asked the onboard system to compose a haiku about its surroundings in space.The satellite received the prompt and generated three lines of poetry. Its subsequent transmission back to Earth confirmed that the system had successfully processed the request.Our TPUs just phoned home… from space.In early October, we sent four TPUs into orbit to test whether our AI hardware could operate in space. The initial goal was to see if our chips could turn on, process a prompt, and transmit a response back to Earth.This week, we got our… pic.twitter.com/j8NJx2nWnQ— Google (@Google) October 30, 2026The response read: “Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core.” Google also tested the model with space-themed limericks. Engineers used additional prompts to retrieve telemetry information about the spacecraft’s operating conditions.The demonstration represents an important technical step. It confirms that the satellite can receive instructions from Earth, process them onboard, and return generated information.Radiation poses major challengeThe spacecraft carries four Google TPUs, although its power system allows engineers to operate only one processor at a time. Its electrical generation capacity reaches approximately 1 kilowatt.Power consumption also limits individual operating sessions. Engineers can run a TPU for roughly 20 minutes before the available energy becomes a constraint.Google’s next tests will examine how the processors withstand the harsh conditions of low Earth orbit. These include temperature fluctuations and exposure to space radiation.Radiation presents a particular challenge for conventional computing hardware. High-energy particles can trigger bit flips, changing stored values inside computer memory.Such errors can corrupt calculations without necessarily activating standard monitoring systems. Google previously examined radiation effects using particle accelerators on Earth.Those experiments suggested inference workloads could tolerate radiation better than model training. However, actual orbital testing will help researchers establish how the hardware behaves under continuous exposure.Two satellites planned for 2027Project Suncatcher eventually aims to connect multiple spacecraft into an orbital computing network. items.title: 谷歌的軌道資料中心衛星在太空寫下詩歌
items.originalTitle: Google's orbital data center satellite writes poetry in space
items.originalSummary: Google’s Suncatcher orbital data center prototype began operating and communicating with Earth after being launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket earlier this month. The satellite carries one Google Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) processor, as well as Google DeepMind’s Gemma 4 AI model. As TechCrunch reports , the model’s first task was to write a haiku about being in space. The satellite generates up to 1 kW of electricity and is intended to serve as a testbed for future networks of spacecraft that will perform large AI inference tasks in orbit. At the same time, the TPU’s power consumption allows it to be switched on for about 20 minutes at a time, complicating communication between the satellite and ground stations. Before beginning operations, the spacecraft spent about three weeks undergoing checks of its onboard systems. A Google representative told the publication that the satellite is operating normally. In addition to the poetry task, engineers also asked the spacecraft to report on conditions in its orbit. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . The next stage of testing will assess the chip’s performance under temperature stress and in conditions of space radiation. Google has already tested the TPU on Earth using particle accelerators, but will now examine the actual effects of radiation in space. It can cause so-called bit flips — changes to values stored in memory that can potentially lead to data corruption without triggering conventional monitoring systems. Ground tests indicated that radiation would have little impact on inference, while model training may be more vulnerable. If the TPU installed on Suncatcher confirms its operability, Google plans to launch two more satellites with improved chips in 2027. They will have more powerful energy supplies and are expected to demonstrate optical inter-satellite communication links.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Supplier STMicroelectronics Forecasts Strong Sales on AI, Satellite Boost
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru STMicroelectronics projected robust sales growth for the year as the build-out of data centers to power artificial-intelligence models and the deployment of satellites to provide connectivity services fuel demand for semiconductors. The European chip maker, which counts Apple and Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX among its clients, said 2026 revenue should grow nearly 23% on year to roughly $14.5 billion. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched measure of pricing power--should increase to about 36.4% from 33.9% last year. The company had refrained from providing detailed annual guidance until now , as it embarks on the final quarter, gaining better visibility into what is driving demand. It expects sales of about $4.15 billion this quarter compared with $3.33 billion a year earlier, above a Visible Alpha forecast of nearly $4.12 billion. Its annual sales projection is also above a Visible Alpha forecast of $14.41 billion. Chief Executive Jean-Marc Chery singled out data centers and satellites as key drivers for growth this year. Like other chip makers, STMicroelectronics is reaping the benefits of hundreds of billions of dollars in spending commitments from some of the world's largest tech groups to build out AI infrastructure. STMicroelectronics stock has nearly doubled in value since the year began, riding a wave of investor fervor around AI that lifted global semiconductor stocks. In a sign of how fast demand for chips to power energy-intensive data centers is building up, STMicroelectronics in July projected revenue from data centers above $1 billion in 2026 and well above $2 billion in 2027 compared with prior guidance of about $1 billion and roughly $2 billion, respectively. That marked the second time the company raised its AI forecasts this year. Alongside data centers, space also provides a key revenue stream for STMicroelectronics and other chip makers that supply semiconductors for low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations. The company expects well above $3 billion in revenue between 2026 and 2028 for the supply of equipment to be used in space, a forecast that for now excludes potential benefits from orbital data centers. Low Earth-orbit satellite networks are closer to Earth than traditional constellations, making them ideal to beam low-latency broadband directly to smartphones in parts of the world where cell towers are unavailable. SpaceX's Starlink provides direct-to-device connectivity to users in several countries, including Ukraine, where damage to terrestrial networks because of the war is common. STMicroelectronics had long relied on the automotive industry to generate a significant portion of its sales. Data centers and satellites have allowed the group to diversify its revenue streams and become less tied to carmakers. The auto industry in recent years had slowly been digesting chip inventories it built at the height of the pandemic, weighing on demand for new orders in a blow to STMicroelectronics. historyItems.originalTitle: AI Data Center Supplier Amphenol Jumps On Earnings Beat
historyItems.originalSummary: Burke Wealth Management, an investment management company, released its "Focused Growth Strategy" Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here . The fund delivered strong results in the third quarter of 2026, benefiting from a sharp recovery in enterprise software and solid corporate earnings amid continued market volatility. The composite returned 10.8% net of fees, substantially outperforming the S&P 500 Total Return Index's 2.3% gain, while its year-to-date return reached 20.0%, compared with 12.7% for the benchmark. The firm attributed the quarter's strength partly to investors reassessing the long-term value of enterprise software platforms that can securely connect AI models with proprietary business data. Burke believes these platforms can serve as essential AI "harnesses," providing permissions, security, and context for enterprise applications, although it cautions that AI agents could challenge traditional software business models and seat-based pricing. historyItems.originalTitle: Space Exploration Technologies Corp (SPCX.O) | Stock Price & Latest News
historyItems.originalSummary: Fred Alger Management , an investment management company, released its "Alger Spectra Fund" third-quarter 2026 investor letter. The letter can be downloaded here . During the third quarter of 2026, U.S. equities delivered modest gains, with the S&P 500 advancing 2%. Despite robust corporate earnings and resilient consumer spending, market breadth remained weak as 60% of S&P 500 constituents closed lower. Against this backdrop, the fund lagged the Russell 3000 Growth Index. Class A shares of the fund returned 0.29% without a sales charge and -4.98% with sales charges, compared to 0.45% for the index. Consumer Discretionary and Tech drove the relative performance, whereas Communication Services and Utilities dragged. Macro headwinds weighed on sectors like Energy following oil supply disruptions. On the short side, a position in an IT consulting firm detracted from returns, while a short in an advertising technology company generated positive gains following its weak earnings report and rising competitive threats. Amid these shifting dynamics, the fund continues to prioritize disciplined stock selection to capture long-term opportunities across the expanding AI ecosystem. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.originalTitle: Google and Oracle are partnering to bring Google TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
historyItems.originalSummary: OCI will be the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer Google TPUsLAS VEGAS, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle AI World -- Oracle and Google today announced that Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) will be available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), marking the first time Google TPUs will be offered on a hyperscale cloud platform outside Google. By bringing Google's purpose-built TPUs to OCI's AI compute portfolio, customers gain the flexibility to match their most demanding workloads with infrastructure designed for near-linear scalability and highly optimized economics. "Different AI workloads have different compute needs," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle. "Bringing Google TPUs to OCI gives customers access to multiple leading AI compute architectures in one cloud. That choice gives them the flexibility to choose the right infrastructure for the performance, throughput, and economics of each AI workload."Google TPUs are custom accelerators co-designed with open software to power the entire AI lifecycle—from frontier training and large-scale inference to the multi-step reasoning data demands of agentic AI. OCI will provide the power, cooling, and datacenter networking to deploy Google TPUs at scale within its infrastructure."The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute," said Amin Vahdat, senior vice president and chief technologist, AI & Infrastructure, Google. "TPUs give customers a powerful, purpose-built option for demanding training and inference workloads. Bringing Google TPUs to OCI will give more organizations access to this technology and greater flexibility in how they build and run their most complex AI applications."More AI Compute Options for Every WorkloadAs models grow and production inference demands increase, the performance and economics of every training run and inference request become increasingly important. Google's TPU architecture is designed to maximize AI processing from each watt of electricity, with fast access to model data and rapid communication between chips.Google TPUs can support large-model training and post-training, including dense and mixture-of-experts models (MoE), as well as production inference for reasoning, agentic, and long-context applications. Customers will be able to choose Google TPUs within OCI, optimized for their workloads, performance requirements, and cost objectives.Drawing on more than a decade of custom AI silicon development, Google's TPU portfolio delivers purpose-built compute optimized for massive machine learning workloads. Google's eighth-generation TPU introduces two purpose-built architectures: TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference. TPU 8t cuts frontier model development cycles from months to weeks, delivering nearly 3x the compute performance per pod over the previous generation, while TPU 8i is designed to handle the iterative work of many specialized agents.Google TPUs on OCI will be available in calendar year 2027, ramping over a multi-year period to meet customer needs.Additional ResourcesLearn more about Oracle C

historyItems.originalTitle: OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
historyItems.originalSummary: OpenAI said it is expanding its partnership with Oracle to bring business applications and AI agents into ChatGPT, while also helping power new Oracle offerings, according to an OpenAI announcement published on Oct. 27, 2026. The update extends a relationship that has already moved beyond infrastructure and into enterprise distribution. In its announcement, OpenAI said the companies are working to place Oracle business applications and AI agents inside ChatGPT, and to support new Oracle products through the collaboration. The statement did not include pricing, rollout timing, customer counts or a product launch schedule. The partnership has been building through multiple prior steps. OpenAI said on Aug. 7, 2026 that eligible Oracle Universal Credits can be used to purchase OpenAI API models, Codex and ChatGPT Work through Oracle Marketplace. Oracle also said on Oct. 16, 2026 that its own employees were adopting Enterprise ChatGPT as part of its AI-transformation update, indicating internal use of OpenAI software within the company. The expansion comes against a broader backdrop of joint infrastructure development. Oracle said in a June 11, 2024 announcement with Microsoft and OpenAI that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure would supply additional capacity by extending Microsoft’s Azure AI platform. OpenAI later named Oracle among the initial equity funders in its Jan. 21, 2025 Stargate announcement, which outlined an intention to invest $500 billion in U.S. AI infrastructure over four years. OpenAI then said on July 22, 2025 that it had agreed with Oracle to develop an additional 4.5 gigawatts of U.S. Stargate capacity, taking the total described in that update to more than 5 gigawatts under development and more than 2 million chips. Those figures described planned development, not already completed capacity. Oracle’s current infrastructure page, as of September 2026, said Abilene had delivered 75% of total capacity, while customer delivery at Shackelford and Doña Ana County was scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. That timeline gives the partnership a physical infrastructure layer, while the new OpenAI announcement points to a broader software and distribution tie-up. There were no verified details in the source material on financial terms, revenue impact, exclusivity, or an official launch date for the new ChatGPT integrations. The timing of any further product rollout remains unknown from the supplied material.

The chipmakers will purchase the equity as part of an up to $95 billion stock sale that the Facebook parent intends to kick off in the near future. The fundraising initiative will also include the participation of Broadcom Inc. Meta didn’t specify how much the company is investing, but it stated on Monday that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom together plan to invest $5 billion. That suggests the networking chip giant will buy $1 billion in shares. Nvidia is investing $3 billion as part of a newly expanded partnership that also includes other components. Notably, Meta plans to broaden its use of the chipmaker’s Rubin graphics processing units and Vera central processing units. Companies often deploy the two chips together in Nvidia-designed DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 appliances. Each system includes 72 GPUs and 36 CPUs. Meta also plans to buy more Nvidia networking gear. It will expand its use of the Spectrum-X Ethernet product family, which includes SuperNICs and switches. SuperNICs are chips that connect servers to a data center’s network, while switches coordinate how traffic flows through that network. GPU clusters’ traffic patterns tend to change rapidly. As a result, connectivity bottlenecks sometimes emerge faster than the network can respond to them. Nvidia says that its Spectrum-X Ethernet product series addresses the challenge by checking GPU traffic for anomalies at sub-microsecond time intervals. A microsecond corresponds to one millionth of a second. Another focus of Meta’s planned network investment is Nvidia’s BlueField-4 chip family. The accelerators in the series are designed to speed common networking, storage and cybersecurity tasks. Nvidia will help Meta improve the performance and cost efficiency of its Muse large language model family. The effort will extend to the Facebook parent’s eponymous consumer AI agent. Additionally, Meta plans to explore “collaboration opportunities” related to Nvidia’s recently introduced OpenShell Reference Architecture. It’s a collection of technical resources that makes it easier to run the chipmaker’s OpenShell toolkit. The toolkit runs AI agents in isolated sandboxes designed to mitigate cybersecurity risks. “Nvidia and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions,” said Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang. AMD, which will invest $1 billion in Meta, today revealed that the Facebook parent has adopted its Helios rack design. Helios contains 72 GPUs much like the DGX Vera Rubin NVL72. It’s based on AMD’s latest Instinct MI450 graphics card architecture, Epyc CPUs and Pensando data processing units, which are the chipmaker’s answer to the BlueField-4.

historyItems.summary: A year ago, the answer to “which model should we use?” was simple: whichever frontier model topped the leaderboard that week. Then open models caught up. historyItems.originalTitle: Introducing Cisco Model Foundry: Bringing AI to our partners
historyItems.originalSummary: A year ago, the answer to “which model should we use?” was simple: whichever frontier model topped the leaderboard that week. Then open models caught up. They cost a fraction as much, you could run them where you wanted, and your data stayed yours. Plenty of teams made the switch. Then they pointed those models at real work. An operator reports that R2 lost every route from R1, but ping across the link still works. A security team needs to find the three files in a million-line codebase most likely to hold a vulnerability. An observability team needs to spot the one interface that matters in a week of telemetry. This is where general-purpose models, open or closed, start to struggle. We think the next leap comes from a model that already knows the domain and then learns your customer. That second step runs on your data and your relationships, and it’s where partners lead. Today at Partner Summit, we’re introducing Cisco Model Foundry , a new platform service in Cisco Cloud Control. It gives partners access to Cisco’s purpose-built models and lets them serve those models in customer applications. When the use case calls for it, partners can also fine-tune the models on their customers’ own data, all in one place. Access Cisco’s domain models. Model Foundry opens up the models Cisco has built on four decades of networking, security, and operations knowledge. Several of them previously ran only inside our own products. Browse the catalog, open the Playground, paste in a real problem, and see how each model handles it before you commit. Put them to work. In Model Foundry, you create an API key, set an expiration, choose a model, and you’re connected. The API is OpenAI-compatible, so it plugs into the agents, tools, and workflows you already run. Administrators get tenant-scoped keys, per-model access controls, and full visibility into usage by model, key, and day. Tailor it when it counts. Fine-tuning means taking the knowledge that makes a network or a business unique and training the model on it. It’s built for the large volumes of data that partners and customers already have: configs, log messages, alerts, tickets, and agent traces from thousands of devices. Model Foundry handles the hard parts, from the GPUs to the training pipeline to built-in evaluation that runs the base and tuned models side by side. You see where tuning helped, and where it didn’t, before anything reaches production. Many partners don’t need to fine-tune to get value. A purpose-built Cisco model, served as-is, is built to outperform generic open models on domain work. Fine-tuning is there for the moments when “good” isn’t good enough.

historyItems.originalTitle: Verizon Lifts Outlook, Inks Amazon Deal Worth More Than $2 Billion
historyItems.originalSummary: By Kelly Cloonan Verizon Communications boosted its full-year outlook again as it continues to attract new customers for its postpaid phone service. The mobile carrier also on Monday said it signed a deal valued at more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services to supply dark fiber for agentic and generative artificial-intelligence workloads. The agreement follows a similar deal earlier this year with Alphabet's Google, which was valued at more than $1 billion. "These two contracts are a clear signal that the largest builders of AI infrastructure in the world are choosing Verizon as a strategic connectivity partner," Chief Executive Dan Schulman said during a call with analysts. Schulman said Verizon is in talks with additional hyperscalers, neocloud providers and large enterprise clients to supply fiber connectivity. The company is also seeing momentum with several partners looking to use its network hubs for AI inference and edge computing, he said. Verizon gained a net 406,000 postpaid phone connections in the latest quarter, marking its strongest third-quarter performance on the closely watched metric in five years. Analysts polled by FactSet expected 195,300 postpaid phone net additions. Schulman said the company is gaining loyal, high-value customers as it shifts away from heavy subsidies to focus on other offerings, like its expanded loyalty program and its Simplicity plan, which it rolled out earlier this year. "We are not buying customers. We are winning them on revenue-positive terms and keeping them longer," Schulman said during a call with analysts. The postpaid strength helped Verizon post higher third-quarter profit and revenue. Schulman, who took the helm of Verizon last October, said the latest quarterly results are proof that it's evolved into a structurally different company. "Verizon is in a fundamentally better position operationally, financially and competitively," Schulman said. "Our transformation has taken root and our results show it." The latest results prompted the company to raise its full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter. Verizon now expects adjusted earnings per share of $5.04 to $5.06 for the full year, compared with its prior view of $4.99 to $5.04, and now projects total full-year postpaid phone net additions of about 1.1 million to 1.2 million, up from a previous range of 875,000 to one million. The company also raised its projection for mobility and broadband service revenue growth to be in the upper half of its prior forecast of 2.5% to 3% for the year. Wall Street projects adjusted earnings of $5 per share and postpaid phone net additions of 975,000 for the year. Verizon's third-quarter profit came in at $5.3 billion, or $1.25 a share, compared with $5.06 billion, or $1.17 a share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.31, compared with analyst estimates of $1.27. Revenue ticked up 1.5% to $34.3 billion, compared with analyst estimates of $34.77 billion. Mobility and broadband service revenue rose 2.9% to $23.5 billion. Equipment revenue declined 9%, as consumers continue to hold on to their mobile devices for longer before

historyItems.originalTitle: Exclusive: Inside Unusual Machines' $52 Million Drone Battery Acquisition
historyItems.originalSummary: Order Helps Powerus Scale Production of Autonomous and Counter-Drone Systems to Meet Growing Demand ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 22, 2026 / Unusual Machines, Inc. (NYSE American:UMAC), a leading manufacturer of NDAA-compliant drone components, today announced that it has received a $16.9 million purchase order from Powerus Corporation (Nasdaq:PUSA), a U.S. defense technology company focused on autonomous and unmanned systems. The order covers critical drone components, including motors, batteries, cameras, and video transmitters (VTX), for use across Powerus’s unmanned systems portfolio “The need for effective autonomous and counter-drone systems is growing rapidly, and Powerus is turning that urgency into action,” said Allan Evans, CEO of Unusual Machines. “This latest order builds on our partnership and underscores the importance of a reliable domestic supply chain behind those systems.” The order expands the companies’ commercial relationship as Powerus scales production to meet growing demand. It follows a previous order exceeding $5 million, announced in April 2026, and a $30 million strategic equity investment by Unusual Machines in Powerus, disclosed in June 2026. “The autonomous systems we deliver to our global customers support missions across incredibly complex and evolving operating environments,” said Brett Velicovich, Co-founder and President at Powerus. “Working with Unusual Machines in the U.S. means we can deliver critical products faster and more affordably to our customers, no matter where they are.” Unusual Machines is a leading provider of NDAA-compliant drone components, focused on building a domestic supply chain for the growing U.S. drone industry. The Company manufactures a broad portfolio of critical components, including flight controllers, electronic speed controllers, video systems, motors, FPV headsets, cameras and, following its acquisition of Upgrade Energy, batteries and power systems. Unusual Machines is expanding U.S. manufacturing to meet increasing demand from defense, enterprise, and commercial customers, while serving the consumer FPV market through its Fat Shark and Rotor Riot brands. According to Fact.MR, the U.S. drone components market represents a $3 billion to $5 billion opportunity. For more information, visit unusualmachines.com . Powerus Corporation (formerly Aureus Greenway Holdings Inc., Nasdaq:PUSA) builds and scales unified autonomous systems designed to move, protect, and sustain critical assets in high-risk environments, with capabilities spanning heavy-lift platforms, autonomous air systems, autonomous maritime systems, mission systems, training and support, and U.S.-based manufacturing. Powerus Corporation also owns and manages two golf courses in the Orlando, Florida region. On October 1, 2026, Powerus completed its previously announced merger with AGH; shares continue trading on Nasdaq under the symbol PUSA. Learn more at power.us. Investor: investors@unusualmachines.com Media: media@unusualmachines.com Investor Relations: Santosh Patel ir@power.us 404-314-8141

historyItems.originalSummary: Ariel Investments , an investment management company, released its "Ariel Appreciation Fund" Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here . Copy main article 1st para. The Fund faced a challenging third quarter of 2026 as rising interest rates, higher energy prices, persistent inflation, and geopolitical uncertainty weighed on mid-cap equities, despite gains in the broader U.S. market. The Fund's Investor Class returned -3.90%, underperforming the Russell Midcap Value Index, which declined 1.98%, and the Russell Midcap Index, which fell 3.00%. Strong earnings, improved guidance, and better operating performance supported several holdings, while concerns about near-term demand, margins, and execution pressured others. The portfolio also experienced weakness in cruise-related and food-equipment businesses, reflecting softer travel trends, higher fuel costs, inflationary pressures, and investor concerns about near-term profitability. During the quarter, the Fund exited its position in a cruise operator and redeployed the proceeds into another major cruise company, sold an electronic-payments holding, and added exposure to a security, residential technology, and fire-safety distribution business following its spin-off. The Fund also received shares in a newly separated food-processing business. Looking ahead, Ariel expects volatility to persist as inflation, monetary policy, and economic growth remain uncertain. The firm views market dislocations as opportunities to acquire quality businesses trading below intrinsic value, emphasizing durable competitive advantages, strong balance sheets, cash generation, and long-term earnings potential. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.title: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 股票下跌，那麼現在是什麼引起了人們的關注呢？
historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) just laid out an aggressive service readiness push, outlining plans to light up satellite cellular coverage across the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia before the end of 2026. For investors, the story around AST SpaceMobile has been far more volatile than the service roadmap. The share price has fallen 5.21% over the last session, is down 39.13% over the past month and 53.55% year to date, yet the three year total shareholder return is extremely high. This suggests long term backers have already experienced very large gains even as recent selling points to rising concern about execution risk and timing around this rollout.

historyItems.originalTitle: TTM Technologies Fiscal Q3 non-GAAP Earnings, Revenue Rise; Initiates Fiscal 2027 Preliminary Outlook
historyItems.originalSummary: Interested in TTM Technologies, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better. TTM Technologies delivered record third-quarter results: Revenue rose 60% year over year to $1.2 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share more than doubled to $1.46. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 20.1% from 16.1%, driven by stronger volume, favorable product mix and execution gains. Data Center & Networking led growth, with sales up 115% and accounting for 41% of revenue, as demand increased for higher-value N+M circuit boards. Aerospace and defense also remained strong, with a record $2 billion backlog and a 1.6 book-to-bill ratio. TTM raised its 2026 outlook to $4.47 billion-$4.49 billion in revenue and issued preliminary 2027 guidance of $6.5 billion-$6.75 billion. The company is planning an additional $400 million capacity investment and pursuing acquisitions, including the proposed $650 million purchase of Ophir Optics.

historyItems.originalTitle: LRCX: Record revenue and earnings, with December-quarter guidance for $8.60B revenue
historyItems.originalSummary: Revenue: $8.22 billion, up 22% sequentially and 54% year-over-year; fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue. Gross Margin: Record 52.4%, up from 52% in the June quarter on favorable customer and product mix. Operating Margin: Record 40.2%, up from 38.4% in the June quarter; first time topping 40%. Diluted EPS: Record $2.20; diluted share count ~1.26 billion. Operating Expenses: $1 billion, up from $916 million prior quarter; R&D ~two-thirds of total. Deferred Revenue: $2.66 billion, up $227 million from the June quarter. Memory Systems Revenue: 46% of systems revenue (record dollar level), up 120% year-over-year; NAND 26% of systems revenue (up from 23%), NAND dollars up ~40% sequentially; DRAM 20% of systems revenue (down from 23%), record dollar level. Foundry Systems Revenue: Record; 46% of systems revenue, up from 44% in the June quarter. Logic and Other Systems Revenue: 8% of systems revenue, down from 10% in the June quarter. CSBG Revenue: Fourth consecutive record quarter at nearly $2.5 billion, up slightly sequentially and 40% year-over-year; calendar 2026 growth expected above 30% year-over-year, with over 15% growth expected in calendar 2027.

historyItems.summary: Nokia advances AI-RAN toward commercial deployment and physical AI, launches sovereign agentic AI platform for telco autonomy with NVIDIA Berlin, Germany – Nokia today announced the next step in how it is bringing AI-native networks to commercial reality with NVIDIA, with new capabilities that apply AI within radio processing, support intelligence close to where data is generated and extend governed AI agents for cross-domain network operations. Building on the industry’s first commercial AI-RAN platform, announced in July, AI-RAN is being integrated into live networks and moving closer to deployment.
historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia advances AI-RAN toward commercial deployment and physical AI, launches sovereign agentic AI platform for telco autonomy with NVIDIA
historyItems.originalSummary: Nokia advances AI-RAN toward commercial deployment and physical AI, launches sovereign agentic AI platform for telco autonomy with NVIDIA Berlin, Germany – Nokia today announced the next step in how it is bringing AI-native networks to commercial reality with NVIDIA, with new capabilities that apply AI within radio processing, support intelligence close to where data is generated and extend governed AI agents for cross-domain network operations. Building on the industry’s first commercial AI-RAN platform, announced in July, AI-RAN is being integrated into live networks and moving closer to deployment. Together, Nokia and NVIDIA are creating the real-time network foundation needed for physical-AI applications while giving operators a practical path to improve today’s 5G and 5G Advanced networks and evolve to AI-native 6G. Customer progress moves AI-RAN closer to deployment One year ago, Nokia and NVIDIA formed a partnership to add NVIDIA-powered, commercial-grade AI-RAN products to Nokia’s radio access network portfolio. The companies are now applying AI within the 5G signal-processing chain, including channel estimation, beamforming, multi-user MIMO pairing and scheduling. Nokia AI-native anyRAN software, running on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer, provides a software-defined foundation for integrating AI-powered radio functions that improve network capacity and performance.

historyItems.originalTitle: A possible SpaceX-Tesla merger? Here's what people are saying
historyItems.originalSummary: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter’s third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees,” Musk said. “So it’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation.” The groups have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction — and there’s no guarantee that they will. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this,” he continued. “And particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.” That said, Musk called the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger a “good idea.” He continued: > I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity. And there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the TeraFab, obviously robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity. So I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies. They’ve got to come up with something and then that’s going to be put to the shareholders as a vote. A Tesla-SpaceX merger would be a blockbuster corporate deal creating a mega-entity valued upwards of $3.6 trillion. But combining Musk’s car and energy company with his AI and rocket company would not be without its tradeoffs. A lot depends on which company absorbs the other. To buy SpaceX, Tesla would have to create millions of new stock shares, which for current Tesla owners would mean owning a smaller slice of a much larger pie. SpaceX’s launch goals require tens of billions of dollars every year — extra spending that could drain Tesla’s ability to build new car factories and battery plants. That said, most Wall Street analysts and legal experts believe SpaceX would acquire Tesla (or absorb it through a stock swap) rather than vice versa. Since its IPO, SpaceX has maintained a higher valuation than Tesla. A merger in that direction would allow SpaceX shareholders to hold the majority control of the combined mega-entity. Some Tesla shareholders may balk at this deal. But it would also create one company for those who believe in Musk’s vision of the future — robot cars, humanoid robots, AI super-intelligence, and human habitats on Mars — in which to place their investments. And Tesla shareholder approved Musk’s enormous pay package last year — even after a Delaware judge tossed it over lack of independence. Earlier this month, Barclays published a client note suggesting a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination could be announced ahead of Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting scheduled for December 3, 2026.

"This is definitely the kind of question where I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield."

historyItems.originalTitle: Boeing’s Large 737 Max Jet Secures U.S. Approval
historyItems.originalSummary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has certified Boeing’s 737 MAX 10, the largest aircraft in the 737 MAX family, following a testing program involving nearly 1,000 flights and more than 2,000 flight hours.The approval clears the path for Boeing to begin delivering the 737-10 in the coming months. The aircraft can accommodate up to 230 passengers, making it the highest-capacity model in the company’s single-aisle 737 MAX lineup.The certification follows extensive safety assessments, design reviews, and ground testing. Boeing said the program included 1,000 ground test hours, tens of thousands of pages of documentation and formal reviews with the FAA.The 737-10 is also the first commercial aircraft certified under the full requirements of the 2020 Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act. The law introduced stricter requirements for documenting aircraft safety assessments and evaluating how pilots interact with aircraft systems.New safety requirements applyWhat sets the aircraft apart is its enhanced angle-of-attack system, which Boeing plans to introduce across the 737 MAX family.Angle of attack refers to the angle between an aircraft wing and the airflow approaching it. The measurement helps pilots and onboard systems assess flight conditions, including the risk of an aerodynamic stall.Boeing says the upgraded system is designed to reduce pilot workload. Its introduction across the MAX family makes the 737-10 an important step in the company’s broader aircraft safety program.“Our flight test team ran a disciplined, methodical campaign to validate every system,” said Chris Payne, vice president and general manager of 737 Airplane Development Programs at Boeing Commercial Airplanes.Larger aircraft expands capacityThe 737-10 typically seats between 185 and 210 passengers in a two-class configuration, although its maximum seating capacity reaches 230.The aircraft has a range of up to 3,100 nautical miles (5,740 kilometers). Boeing also claims it offers the lowest cost per seat among single-aisle aircraft currently in service, although that comparison was not independently established in the announcement.According to Boeing, the aircraft offers 365 nautical miles more range than competing aircraft without auxiliary fuel tanks. The company also says technological improvements across the 737 MAX program reduce fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions by 20%, without specifying the comparison baseline in the announcement.Airline interest in the largest MAX variant is substantial. Boeing reported 1,555 orders from more than 30 customers, representing over 30 percent of the program’s outstanding orders.Across the broader 737 MAX family, customers have placed 7,350 orders, with nearly 2,500 aircraft delivered through September 2026. The FAA certified the smaller 737-7 earlier this year. With the 737-10 now approved, Boeing has secured certification for the final member of the MAX family.However, certification does not mean the aircraft has entered commercial service. Boeing expects customer deliveries to begin in the coming months.

historyItems.originalTitle: Boeing wins FAA approval for 737 Max 10 after years of delays as Duffy says certification process should be faster
historyItems.originalSummary: (Bloomberg) -- Boeing Co. won US regulator approval for its 737 Max 10 jet, capping off a lengthy certification saga for the planemaker’s family of narrowbody aircraft that was disrupted by two fatal crashes and a series of quality lapses.The 737 Max 10 is the largest of the company’s single-aisle aircraft and is Boeing’s response to rival Airbus SE’s A321neo. The plane’s 1,500-plus order book makes it one of the more popular Max variants, purchased by US carriers like United Airlines Holdings Inc. and Alaska Air Group Inc. The Max 10’s smallest sibling, the 737 Max 7, was approved by the US Federal Aviation Administration in August.“The FAA’s decision follows a thorough review of the aircraft’s design and safety requirements,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said in a news release, adding that the regulator will “continue to hold Boeing to the highest safety standards” moving forward.Bloomberg reported in July that the FAA was expected to certify the Max 10 around October. The timeline was briefly in doubt after the planemaker disclosed a software glitch with the airplane’s navigation system, but an FAA panel determined the issue did not pose a safety risk.“The 737-10 offers greater capacity, longer range and the best seat economics in its class, a platform that will create more value and opportunities for airlines around the world,” Boeing Commercial Airplanes Chief Executive Officer Stephanie Pope said in a statement Tuesday.The Max 10 is one of Boeing’s most important new jets, offering airlines a solution to replace the out-of-production 757. Alongside the other Max models, the largest variant will help the planemaker repair its balance sheet and pare down debt. The aircraft can seat as many as 230 passengers and fly for up to 3,100 nautical miles, according to Boeing’s website.US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said streamlining aircraft certification is essential to America’s ability to compete with Europe and China, noting that it took nearly a decade to approve the Max 10. “I have to allow you all to certify ​aircraft faster,” Duffy told a ceremony at Boeing’s widebody site north of Seattle on Tuesday. “You have to come to the market more quickly.”Regulators in Canada and Europe are expected to complete their own Max 10 approvals in “probably a couple months,” Mike Sinnett, a Boeing executive over development programs, said later.

historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile Advances Service Readiness Ahead of Initial Space-Based Cellular Broadband Coverage in Key Global Markets
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile, Inc. announced it is advancing service readiness in key global markets before the end of 2026, including the United States, Canada, Japan, United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia. AST SpaceMobile now has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed, or in planning worldwide. The expansive ground network supports AST SpaceMobile?s global commercial ecosystem with over 60 mobile network operators who cover over 3 billion subscribers, bringing a third layer of connectivity directly into the mobile networks people already use.Spectrum is a key component of this readiness. AST SpaceMobile combines strategic partner operators? spectrum with access to mobile satellite services (MSS) spectrum, targeting approximately 100 MHz of access in the United States.Its spectrum position includes access to 45 MHz of MSS mid-band spectrum in North America and priority rights to 60 MHz of S-band spectrum globally on a market-by-market basis. The company?s satellite technology can tune across approximately 1,150 MHz of low- and mid-band frequencies globally, providing flexibility to serve different markets using available partner and satellite spectrum, subject to applicable regulatory approvals. Supporting this service rollout, AST SpaceMobile?s ground network connects the company?s growing satellite constellation with mobile operators?core networks, routing voice, video and broadband data between space and ground-based infrastructure, making it a key component of the end-to-end infrastructure required to deliver space-based cellular broadband connectivity through partners to people everywhere they work, live, and travel. This integration enables operators to extend their reach beyond the limits of terrestrial coverage while evolving alongside future 3GPP standards. In the United States, the Company has already enabled over 3,000 coverage cells and expects to activate the roughly 5,600 cellular cells that cover the continuous United States before year-end.Enabling the remaining digital cells will establish the geographic footprint required to support initial, intermittent service across the contiguous United States and is a prerequisite for nationwide rollout. During this initial phase, service will be available within the satellites? coverage area.Additional spacecraft deployments will extend the duration and frequency of coverage as AST SpaceMobile advances toward continuous service. BlueBird satellites are assembled, integrated, and tested at AST SpaceMobile?s facilities in Midland, Texas, with production now progressing through BlueBird 50. Service availability will expand as satellite capacity and ground infrastructure are deployed and network integration progresses, subject to applicable authorizations.

historyItems.originalTitle: GE Vernova secures order aimed to strengthen regional energy capacity in Côte d’Ivoire
historyItems.originalSummary: Developed by Songon Energies S.A., Songon power plant is built to strengthen energy security and support future growing electricity demand in Greater Abidjan GE Vernova 9E turbine technology to support reliable power delivery for industrial growth and millions of households Infrastructure development expected to create up to 1,400 new jobs and drive positive community impact ABIDJAN, Côte d'Ivoire - [October 20, 2026] - GE Vernova announced today that it will provide the gas power technology forthe new Songon combined-cycle power plant, located in the Songon region near Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. Following the signing of financing agreements last June, Songon Energies- Ivorian development investment company focused on advancing energy infrastructure - selected GE Vernova to supply a 9E gas turbine and generator. The plant - to be built by the EPC contractor China Energy International Engineering Co., Ltd. - is expected to deliver 372 megawatts (MW), a capacity equal to the power needs of approximately 5 million Ivorian homes. Supporting a growing national energy landscape. Côte d'Ivoire has made significant progress, reaching an electrification rate of 94.3 percent by 2024 through initiatives like the "Electricity for All Program" (PEPT), in line with the national goal to achieve universal electrification and improved power quality by 2030. Despite these gains, the nation faces an annual demand growth rate of 10 to 15 percent and rural areas still require expanded access. In this energy landscape, this new power plant will help fill a critical gap. The facility is projected to represent up to 12 percent of the country's total installed base upon its scheduled 2029 operational launch, playing a vital role in meeting these ambitious development targets. Furthermore, the project is expected to generate up to 1,400 new jobs, creating economic opportunities for the local community. "The Songon Energies project is designed to strengthen energy security and support future growing electricity demand growth in the Greater Abidjan region while reinforcing the country's position as a regional energy hub in West Africa," said Mr. Wang Xiaoming, Deputy General Manager (Acting CEO) for Songon Energies. "The facility is expected to ease energy pressure on the Abidjan metropolitan area, providing a reliable foundation for the development of skilled workers, the growth of industrial zones, the expansion of small and medium-sized enterprises, and a tangible improvement in the daily lives of millions of Ivorian households. We selected to work with GE Vernova for this new power plant, because of our deep trust in their efficient technology and their constant, proven presence in Côte d'Ivoire, which gives us great confidence in the long-term success of this facility."
